OSCE"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"https:\/\/nagameghana68.blogspot.com\/\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EOSCE\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E1.How sugar turns into fat in liver?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cp class=\"rt-p\"\u003ESince your body can only store\u0026nbsp; required glycogen, if you eat a lot of sugar more than your muscles and liver can hold at one time—your body needs another place to put the excess. In that case, it converts that extra glucose into fat through a chemical process called lipogenesis.\u0026nbsp;This fat is stored under the skin (subcutaneous fat), around your\u0026nbsp;abdominal\u0026nbsp;organs (visceral fat), or in\u0026nbsp;certain\u0026nbsp;other organs such as your liver. If glycogen is like a checking account, then fat is your body’s savings account. It hangs onto this fat in case you use up your glycogen stores.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"rt-p\"\u003ESugar isn’t the only compound your body can turn into fat. If you eat too much protein, the extra protein gets stored as fat, too. Like sugar, protein contains calories, so if you take in more calories than you burn, the excess protein is converted first into glycogen and then into fat. Still, you’re more likely to store sugar as fat than protein.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2.\u003Cb\u003EHow does visceral fat leads to chronic kidney disease?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIncreased visceral fat accumulation causes adipose tissue inflammation and adipokine dysregulation , which can lead to dyslipidemia, insulin resistance,\u0026nbsp;renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) overactivation\u0026nbsp;,\u0026nbsp;sodium retention ,extracellular fluid volume expansion.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIncreased visceral fat accumulation is also accompanied with perirenal and renal sinus fat accumulation, which causes high intrarenal pressure, which leads to compression of the vasa recta capillaries and thin loops of Henle, reduced blood flow in the renal medulla, increased sodium reabsorption in the loop of Henle, RAAS activation, and increased sodium reabsorption\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThese pathological conditions interact in a complex manner, ultimately damaging the kidneys by causing glomerular hyperfiltration\u0026nbsp;and inflammation\u0026nbsp;both of which are characteristics of obesity-related kidney disease.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003ELearning points\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELearnt about how\u0026nbsp; visceral fat causes health problems\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELearnt the mechanism how the food we take is converted to fat\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELearnt the relation between visceral fat and parotidomegaly\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELearnt about how Diabetes effects all the organs\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELearnt about relation between hypertension and kidney
